alignments.note: The participle's object is accusative, which English realizes with no preposition, so the *of* of *ignorant of* is the predicate's own government and stays inside this unit (rules 21, 106).
Outer article governing δικαιοσύνην across the interposed genitive (rule 57); the ASV writes *God's righteousness*, so the determiner slot is occupied by the possessor and rule 20 empties it.
Inner article of the possessor; the ASV writes a bare *God's* with no determiner, so nothing anchors it (rules 23, 57).
Genitive name rendered with the English prenominal possessive.
ἴδιος is substantival here, governing no expressed head noun, so the article supplies the pronoun *their* and the adjective keeps *own* (rules 47, 54).
Bare infinitive with no governing conjunction, so the infinitival *to* is its own verb's helper (rules 7, 61).
The article takes the English determiner and the dative's case preposition rides with it (rule 21).
Article before θεοῦ with no English determiner; rule 21's determinerless clause leaves *of* with the noun and empties the article.
Source noun rendered *of + noun*; rule 17 heads on the noun.

Passive rendered reflexively; subject, auxiliary and the reflexive *themselves* are rule 7 and 9 helpers, headed on the lexical verb. Discontinuous under rule 15, the intervening *not* belonging to οὐχ.

review_notes: Both articles of the first phrase are emptied: the outer by the prenominal possessor (rule 20 via rule 57), the inner because the ASV writes no determiner on *God's*.
τήν before ἰδίαν takes the pronoun because ἴδιος governs no expressed head noun (rule 47).
